homeCoverage.title: Where the data comes from
homeCoverage.lead: Every country publishes its data its own way: a register to download here, an API to query there, formats and uptime with nothing in common. {{siteName}} deals with that and returns the same answer either way. More sources are added as integrations land.
homeCoverage.tableCaption: Official sources we query, by country
homeCoverage.euWhy: The European verification service, for numbers no national register covers yet.
homeCoverage.beWhy: The VAT number is the enterprise number: 1.9 M entities.
homeCoverage.czWhy: ARES publishes the DIČ, so one call resolves the number.
homeCoverage.deWhy: A self-declared directory, unverified: the status stays unknown.
homeCoverage.dkWhy: The VAT number is the CVR number, and the register is complete.
homeCoverage.eeWhy: The daily file carries the VAT number itself.
homeCoverage.elWhy: AADE first, then GEMI, searchable by AFM, which is the VAT number itself.
homeCoverage.fiWhy: The full trade register, plus the API for ceased companies.
homeCoverage.frWhy: Millions of legal units in our database, addresses included.
homeCoverage.hrWhy: The OIB is the VAT number, resolved with no derivation.
homeCoverage.lvWhy: The VAT payers register joined with the business register.
homeCoverage.plWhy: Resolved on demand on the first request, then served from the stored answer.
homeCoverage.roWhy: ANAF returns the identity, the seat and the VAT status by CUI.
homeCoverage.auWhy: The ABN, its GST registration, and an address that stops at state and postcode.
homeCoverage.brWhy: The whole register every month, and every edition kept since 2023.
homeCoverage.caWhy: The federal register, keyed by the business number the GST/HST number is built on; federal corporations only.
homeCoverage.ruWhy: Keyed by the ИНН an invoice carries; small and medium-sized businesses only, and no address finer than the town.
homeCoverage.uaWhy: Keyed by the ЄДРПОУ the twelve-digit ІПН on an invoice reduces to; companies only, and the register publishes no address and no VAT status.
homeCoverage.jpWhy: The register of consumption-tax invoice issuers: being in it is what the number means.
homeCoverage.sgWhy: The UEN identifies the entity, address included; it says nothing about GST.
homeCoverage.crWhy: Name and tax status by cédula jurídica; the register publishes no address at all.
homeCoverage.ilWhy: The company number is the number it invoices under: 730,000 companies, addresses included.
homeCoverage.peWhy: The whole taxpayer register, rebuilt daily; the district stays a code SUNAT publishes no table for.
homeCoverage.twWhy: Both registers, companies and sole traders, seat address included and no key needed.
homeCoverage.noWhy: Keyed by the organisasjonsnummer, with the seat address and, uniquely outside the Union, the VAT register’s own verdict on the number.
homeCoverage.chWhy: Keyed by the nine digits of the UID, with the registered seat and whether the MWST entry is live; capped at twenty calls a minute.
homeCoverage.vnWhy: The tax administration puts a captcha on its own lookup, so Vietnamese answers come from an aggregator of its data, named as one.
homeCoverage.ngWhy: Keyed by either generation of the TIN; the service publishes a name and no address or status, and the company register is unreachable.
homeCoverage.ecWhy: Keyed by the RUC on the invoice, with the head office address read from a second endpoint the register keeps the premises in.
homeCoverage.glWhy: Greenland levies no VAT and keeps no register: since the GER was dissolved in 2018 its companies sit in the Danish CVR, and the seat is what tells the two countries apart.
homeCoverage.nzWhy: One number every agency quotes, with the entity type and every current address; it is not the IRD number, which is not public.

homeUsecases.title: Four common uses
homeUsecases.c1Text: An invalid number or a struck-off company is caught before the invoice goes out. The answer carries the register that replied and the date it said so, which is what documents a reverse charge the day someone asks for it.
homeUsecases.c2Text: One call returns everything the sources have already said about a number, each answer dated. A change of legal name, a move, a company that stopped trading: what moved reads straight off, with no two exports to compare by hand.
homeUsecases.c3Text: The user types their VAT number and the rest of the form fills itself: legal name, address, national identifier. Five fewer inputs, the typos that came with them, and an address written the way the register writes it.
homeUsecases.c4Text: Replay your account base to normalise legal names and addresses, and spot companies that are no longer active. The national identifier on each account is also what ties it back to your billing.

pricingFaq.title: The questions we get
pricingFaq.q1: What is the difference between the two plans?
pricingFaq.a1: How many requests a month, how many monitors you get, and the audit trail: Pro keeps it for {{auditProDays}} days, Free does not include it. The endpoints, the fields, the country coverage and the response envelope are identical.
pricingFaq.a2: Every answer this API gives you is kept as it was sent, so that months later you can produce what we told you about a VAT number: the company, the register it came from, and which edition of which file. You read it in the console, or over GET /v1/audit to put it inside your own application; either way it costs no quota. It is a Pro feature, kept {{auditProDays}} days. A Free account sees its last {{auditFreeKeep}} answers, enough to see the page working, with nothing kept beyond that.
pricingFaq.a3: A call to GET /v1/lookup/{number} that receives an answer. A 400 format error is not counted, since a malformed number is rejected before any source is consulted; neither is a 503, where a source failed to answer. GET /v1/countries and GET /health never count.
pricingFaq.q4: What happens when the quota runs out?
pricingFaq.a4: The API answers 429 with the same error envelope as every other code. Nothing is billed on overage: calls resume when the monthly quota renews at the start of the next month.
pricingFaq.q5: Do I need a card to get started?
pricingFaq.a5: No. The Free plan takes an email address and gives you {{quotaFree}} requests a month, for as long as you like.
pricingFaq.a6: {{pricePro}} € excluding VAT per month, billed monthly. A compliant invoice is issued on every payment, and the reverse charge applies to VAT-registered customers outside France.
pricingFaq.a7: Yes, with no notice and no fee. The subscription stays active until the end of the period you already paid for, then falls back to the Free plan.
pricingFaq.q8: Where does the data come from?
pricingFaq.a8: From official national registers wherever one can be keyed by a VAT number: SIRENE for France, the KBO for Belgium, the Sudski registar for Croatia… A member state that publishes neither an importable file nor an API of its own is served through VIES, with caching and a retry strategy to absorb its outages. GET /v1/countries answers with the current list, which is the authoritative one.
pricingFaq.q9: Is the data up to date?
pricingFaq.a9: Every answer carries meta.source, the register that answered, and meta.sourceDate, the day it said so: the publication date of the file for a register we import, the day of the call for one we query live. So you never have to assume.

docs.title: API documentation · {{siteName}}
docs.description: Full reference for the Vatlas API: authentication, GET /v1/lookup/{vatNumber}, GET /v1/countries, response envelope, error codes and samples in cURL, JavaScript, Python and PHP.

docsIntro.text: One REST API, three entry points, one JSON envelope. Everything is a GET, everything is UTF-8, and every date is UTC in ISO 8601.
docsIntro.baseUrlText: Paths are versioned (/v1/…). A version never changes shape in a breaking way: a new field may appear, none is ever removed.

docsAuth.title: Authentication
docsAuth.text: Every call carries a key as a bearer token in the Authorization header. You can create as many keys as you like: they all draw on the same account quota, and are there to tell you which of your integrations made a call.
docsAuth.calloutText: It must never ship in a front-end bundle: anyone could read it and burn your quota. Proxy the call through your backend.
docsAuth.after: A missing, unknown or revoked key answers 401 with the standard error envelope, and is not counted. Create your key: the Free plan is free and needs no card.

docsEnvelope.title: Response envelope
docsEnvelope.text: Success always carries data and meta. An error always carries error, and meta when there is something to add to it. The shape does not change with the register the data came from: your code has nothing to branch on.
docsEnvelope.l2: meta.sourceDate: the last day that register was seen saying it, and meta.sourceSince the first: the publication date of the file for an imported register, the day of the call for a live one.
docsEnvelope.l3: meta.sourceUpdatedAt: UTC timestamp of the data served. On a vies answer it can be older than the call itself: when neither VIES nor the register will answer at all, the last answer we hold is served rather than a 503. This field says when it was checked.
docsEnvelope.l4: meta.proof: the proof that the check was made: { "type": "vies_consultation_number", "value": "…" }. A consultation number is what a tax authority accepts as evidence. Present on every answer that came from VIES and on no other: a national register issues nothing of the kind, so the key is absent rather than null. It is an object and not a bare string, so reading type is all your code has to do.
docsEnvelope.l5: meta.checkedAt: on a VAT_NOT_REGISTERED error only: the instant VIES gave that answer when we asked it for this request, and the day it said so when the answer came from what we already held.

docsLookup.title: Resolve a VAT number
docsLookup.text: The heart of the API. Input is normalised before validation: case, spaces, dots and dashes are ignored, and Greece's ISO prefix GR is accepted alongside its VAT prefix EL. data.vatNumber always comes back in canonical form.
docsLookup.paramDesc: Intra-community VAT number, country prefix included. FR08000325175 and fr 08 000.325-175 are equivalent.
docsLookup.preferParamDesc: What to favour when the sources disagree: completeness, the default, takes the fullest answer among every source the country has; proof answers only when the answer carries a proof, skipping the stored history and every source that issues no verification code. Any other value is a 400.
docsLookup.proofText: When the answer comes from VIES rather than from a register, meta carries one field more. proof.value is the consultation number VIES issued for that check, the identifier a tax authority accepts as evidence that the number was verified on that day. We ask for one on every call; when VIES issues none, the answer is still served, without meta.proof. Keep the value with the invoice it justifies.
docsLookup.calloutTitle: An empty name is not a bug.
docsLookup.calloutText: Germany and Spain disclose neither legal name nor address through VIES. Germany is answered from the Peppol e-invoicing directory where the company is listed there; the name is self-declared, hence status: unknown. Otherwise, and for Spain, only status is meaningful.
docsLookup.requireText: Which source answers is normally ours to decide, and by default we take the fullest answer among every source the country has, most of the time a national register we have already imported: rich, fast, and with nothing to prove it. ?prefer=proof turns that around: the stored history and every source that issues no verification code are skipped, and you are answered only if the answer carries meta.proof.
docsLookup.requireCost: It costs one request, like a plain lookup. The real cost is time, since a live VIES call goes out every time, and one more way to fail: 503 PROOF_UNAVAILABLE, when VIES answers and issues no consultation number, which is what it does for most numbers it reports as unregistered. Like every 503, it is not billed. Answers are kept in your audit trail with their consultation number.
docsLookup.historyParamDesc: A flag: write ?history to be given everything the source that answered has ever said, under a history node beside data and meta. Off by default, since it is one query more and most integrations read the answer alone.

docsLookupAll.title: Every source's answer
docsLookupAll.text: The endpoint above answers “what is this number”, and stops at the first source that names a company. This one answers “what has every register said about this number, and when”: it publishes each source’s whole history, calls any live source whose last statement has gone stale, and reports that call’s failure when it fails. Nothing is skipped as redundant, because a report with a hole in it proves nothing. Each entry is a lookup (data and meta, or error and meta where that source has nothing), so code that reads the endpoint above reads these without a second shape to learn.
docsLookupAll.paramDesc: Same number, same normalisation as the plain lookup. Only the path differs.
docsLookupAll.statusText: So the status line is about the report and not about the number: 200 as soon as the number parses, even when every source failed. The verdicts live one level down, in data.sources. Only a malformed number is a 400, and it costs nothing.
docsLookupAll.fSource: The register, inside meta: SIRENE, ARES, MF_WL, PEPPOL, GEMI, VIES… with name beside it, as its publisher writes it.
docsLookupAll.countTitle: How many entries come back depends on the country.
docsLookupAll.countText: A source that does not exist here produces no entry at all. France has no live national register; Bulgaria has no file to import; a register whose credentials this deployment does not hold is absent entirely. There is nothing to prove about a register that was never going to be asked. A source that exists and has never held this number is listed all the same, with an error saying it holds nothing.
docsLookupAll.fKind: bulk for a register we import as a file, live for one we call, both for the four that offer each. A register that is both is listed once: it has one history, read two ways.
docsLookupAll.fCall: Inside meta, present exactly when this request made a live call, which is when the stored history had aged past a week. Its status is that call’s verdict (found, not-registered, not-found or unavailable), and an unavailable carries error.fault and error.attempts, which are what tell a source outage from a rate limit.
docsLookupAll.fHistory: What this source has said, oldest first, and absent under ?history=false. One entry per uninterrupted stretch during which it said the same thing, bounded by from and to, so a company that has not moved since 2019 is one entry spanning seven years rather than eighty. A gap between one entry and the next means no file was read in between.
docsLookupAll.fStatement: Each entry carries from and to, the stretch over which that source kept saying it (the publication dates of the files for an imported register, the days of the calls for a live one), then the company in the same shape the plain lookup publishes, file when it was read out of one, and proof on a positive VIES entry.
docsLookupAll.historyParamDesc: On here, unlike on the plain lookup: ?history=false drops the history node from every entry, and saves the query it costs. What is left is the statement in force for each source, which is what a comparison between registers reads.
docsLookupAll.fData: The company as this source describes it today, meaning its statement in force, in the exact shape the plain lookup publishes. Absent when that source has nothing to show, where error takes its place.
docsLookupAll.fError: In place of data: VAT_NOT_REGISTERED when this source says the number is not registered, SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE when the call this request made did not come back (with fault and attempts), COMPANY_NOT_FOUND when the source has never said anything about it.
docsLookupAll.fMeta: Where the answer comes from and how fresh it is, exactly as on the plain lookup, plus name and kind (the register as its publisher writes it, and how we read it), and call when this request made a live call.

docsFields.title: Response fields
docsFields.caption: Fields of data
docsFields.countryCode: Two-letter VAT prefix (EL for Greece, XI for Northern Ireland).
docsFields.nationalNumber: The national part of the number, without the prefix.
docsFields.nationalId: Identifier in the national register (SIREN, Business ID, registrikood…). May differ from the VAT number.
docsFields.name: Legal name as published by the source. Empty string when the source does not disclose it.
docsFields.legalForm: Legal form as the originating register publishes it, in its own language and not harmonised across countries. Where the register publishes a code alone (France, Czechia, Belgium) the label is resolved for you.
docsFields.line1: Street, or the whole address when the source does not split it.
docsFields.city: Town. null for Latvia, whose register publishes a territory code.

docsMonitor.addText: Answers 201. Following the same number twice answers 409.
docsMonitor.addUrl: Callbacks go to the default URL set in your console. To send this one somewhere else, pass a url in the body:
docsMonitor.deleteText: Answers 204. The delivery history goes with it.
docsMonitor.eventText: data and meta are the same envelope as a plain lookup, so a client that already reads GET /v1/lookup/{vatNumber} needs nothing new. previous is what you were last told.
docsMonitor.firstCheck: The first check after you add a monitor never sends an event: it records the current state, so the next change has something to compare against.
docsMonitor.getText: Returns the monitor, what it last saw, and its recent delivery attempts.
docsMonitor.limit: Monitors do not count against your monthly quota. Your plan caps how many companies you can follow at once.
docsMonitor.listText: Returns every monitor on the account. meta.limit is how many your plan allows.
docsMonitor.text: Follow a company by its VAT number and receive a callback when a register changes its name, status or address. Useful for keeping a supplier or customer file current without re-checking every number yourself.
docsMonitor.title: Monitor

docsAsync.cancelText: Answers 204. The request already spent is not credited back.
docsAsync.cost: One request off your monthly quota, taken when you queue it. If no source ever answers, the lookup is given up on and the request is credited back.
docsAsync.failed: If it is given up on, you receive lookup.failed with an error object instead, so you are never left waiting on silence.
docsAsync.getText: Returns the lookup, every attempt made so far and, once there is one, the result. Costs no quota.
docsAsync.listText: Newest first. Filter with ?status=pending|success|failed, page with ?limit= and ?before=. Costs no quota.
docsAsync.queueAllText: The same thing for every source at once, each answering for itself. Also 202, also one request.
docsAsync.queueText: Answers 202: nothing is resolved yet. Add ?prefer=proof to ask for a lookup with proof. Pass a url in the body to override your default callback URL.
docsAsync.resultText: data and meta are exactly what the synchronous call would have returned, so the same parsing works for both.
docsAsync.text: When no source can answer for a number right away, queue the lookup instead of retrying yourself. Vatlas retries it at several points during the day, then over the following days, and sends you the result as soon as it gets one.
docsAsync.title: Lookup Async

docsCallbacks.evChanged: A register changed what it says about a company you follow.
docsCallbacks.evCompleted: A queued lookup got an answer.
docsCallbacks.evFailed: A queued lookup was given up on.
docsCallbacks.evTest: You pressed “Send a test event” in the console. Same format, invented data.
docsCallbacks.requestText: Answer 2xx and we consider it delivered. The body is JSON; the event name is in the body and in the X-Vatlas-Event header. X-Vatlas-Delivery is unique per attempt, so you can use it to ignore a duplicate.
docsCallbacks.retriesText: A delivery that does not answer 2xx is retried a few times over the next few seconds. Every attempt, successful or not, is listed in the console with the status your endpoint returned. That is the first place to look if something never arrived.
docsCallbacks.secret: Your signing secret is on the Monitor page in the console, where you can also roll it. One secret covers both features.
docsCallbacks.signatureConstantTime: Compare the two in constant time if your language offers it, and reject the request if they differ, or if t is more than a few minutes old, which is what stops someone replaying a request they captured earlier.
docsCallbacks.signatureIntro: Every request we send carries an X-Vatlas-Signature header. It has two parts separated by a comma: t, the unix time we sent it, and v1, a hash of the request made with your signing secret. Here is what arrives:
docsCallbacks.signatureStep1: Take t, a full stop, and the raw request body, exactly the bytes you received, before parsing them. A body that has been through a JSON parser and back is not the same string, and the hash would no longer match. That gives you what was signed:
docsCallbacks.signatureStep2: Compute the HMAC-SHA256 of that string with your signing secret, and compare it with v1:
docsCallbacks.signatureTitle: Checking a webhook signature (Monitor, Lookup Async)
docsCallbacks.test: Before a company you follow ever changes, use “Send a test event” in the console: a real signed request to your real URL, carrying invented data in the exact format of a real event.
docsCallbacks.text: Monitor and Lookup Async both deliver by POSTing JSON to a URL you choose. Each has its own default URL in the console, and any single monitor or lookup can override it.
docsCallbacks.title: Callbacks

docsAudit.title: Audit trail
docsAudit.text: Every answer we have given you, as it was sent, so you can produce it again months later: what we said about a VAT number, which register it came from and on what date that register said it. The same history the console shows, over HTTP.
docsAudit.free: On the Free plan this endpoint returns your last {{auditFreeKeep}} answers, which is enough to see the feature working. Pro keeps the full history for {{auditProDays}} days.
docsAudit.cost: It costs no quota. These answers were counted when they were produced.
docsAudit.pVat: One number’s history. Normalized like everywhere else, so spacing and case do not matter. Omit it for your most recent calls, newest first.
docsAudit.pBefore: Cursor: pass the meta.nextBefore of the previous page, that is the publicId of its last row, to get the next one. null means there is no next page. A cursor that is not one of your own rows is a 400.
docsAudit.idNote: publicId is a UUIDv7: it is the value to pass back as before to get the next page.
docsAudit.responseNote: response is the envelope exactly as it was sent at the time, the error body for a 404 or a 503 included: it is the record of what you were told, not a fresh answer.

docsCountries.title: List every country and how it is served
docsCountries.text: Returns every prefix the service answers for, 39 in all, with the source behind each and its strategy: bulk for an imported register, on-demand for the register's own API, both, or vies for a member state with no usable local source, which still resolves through the VIES fallback.

docsHealth.title: Liveness probe
docsHealth.text: Answers only once a database round trip has succeeded, so it works as-is for a readiness probe. This call costs no quota.

docsErrors.title: Error codes
docsErrors.text: Every error shares the same shape:
docsErrors.caption: Error codes
docsErrors.invalid: Invalid syntax or checksum; no source was consulted. reason says which: EMPTY, UNKNOWN_COUNTRY, BAD_FORMAT, BAD_CHECKSUM.
docsErrors.missingKey: No Authorization: Bearer credential was sent, or the header used another scheme. This call is not counted against your quota.
docsErrors.invalidKey: The key is unknown or has been revoked. Revoking a key takes effect within a minute, so a key revoked seconds ago may still answer.
docsErrors.quota: The monthly quota for the account is spent. It renews at the start of the next month; X-RateLimit-Reset carries the exact instant.
docsErrors.notRegistered: VIES gave a definitive answer: the number is not registered for intra-community trade. A company can be perfectly active in its national register without an intra-community VAT registration. The response carries meta.checkedAt and the same meta.proof as a positive answer.
docsErrors.notFound: Nothing left to ask: the number is valid, but was found nowhere.
docsErrors.unavailable: Nothing stored answers, and no live source could be reached. This is not a negative result and is never stored: retry later.
docsErrors.proofUnavailable: Only with ?prefer=proof: the check was made and VIES issued no consultation number, so it cannot be proved. This says nothing about the number: there may well be a good answer behind it, which is what asking for a proof declines to accept. Retry, or ask for ?prefer=completeness to take the answer unproved.
docsErrors.invalidQuery: A query parameter is out of range or malformed: prefer with a value other than completeness or proof, history with a value other than true or false, or on /v1/audit a limit outside 1-100 or a before that is not a cursor we handed you. The request is rejected rather than quietly corrected.
docsErrors.sourceError: A source failed in a way that is not an outage. It only ever appears inside data.sources on /v1/lookup-all, never as the status of a request.
docsErrors.invalidBody: The JSON body is not an object, or one of its fields is of the wrong type. A boolean has a spelling in JSON, and "true" is not it.
docsErrors.callbackMissing: Neither the monitor nor the account names a callback URL, so there is nowhere to deliver. Refused at creation rather than discovered days later.
docsErrors.invalidCallback: The callback URL is not absolute, is not http or https, carries credentials, or points at an address this service will not call.
docsErrors.monitorLimit: Your plan follows a fixed number of companies at a time, and it is reached. Every listing reports the ceiling as meta.limit.
docsErrors.monitorExists: This account already follows that number. Following it twice would deliver the same event twice.

docsQuotas.title: Quotas & limits
docsQuotas.text: The quota is monthly and belongs to the account, not to an individual key. Every metered response carries the current state of the counter, so there is nothing to estimate:
docsQuotas.l1: A 400 format error is never counted: the number is rejected before any source is consulted.
docsQuotas.l2: A 503 is not counted either: a source failed to answer, and that is not your call to pay for.
docsQuotas.l3: /v1/countries and /health need no key and cost no quota; /v1/audit needs one and costs none either.
docsQuotas.l4: Quota exhausted: 429, with the same error envelope. X-RateLimit-Reset says when it renews.
docsQuotas.after: Plan details on the pricing page.

benchmarks.title: Benchmarks · {{siteName}}
benchmarks.description: Measured response times and field completeness of the {{siteName}} API, globally and country by country, from the last benchmark run.
benchmarks.h1: What the API answers, and how fast
benchmarks.lead: Figures from a real run against the API: latency percentiles, and how often each field comes back filled. Everything here is read from the summary the benchmark writes.
benchmarks.error: The benchmark figures could not be loaded.
benchmarks.noscript: The figures are read from a JSON file, so this page needs JavaScript.
benchmarks.method: Latency is measured end to end, from the request leaving the benchmark to the response being parsed, one lookup at a time. Answered is the share of lookups the API answered: a company returned, or a register stating the number is not registered; the rest are timeouts and unreachable sources. Completeness is counted over the lookups that returned a company.

benchmarksCompleteness.title: Completeness, all countries together
benchmarksCompleteness.lead: How often each field of a returned record is actually filled. A country that discloses only a name caps every other figure.

benchmarksPerCountry.title: Country by country
benchmarksPerCountry.lead: Only the countries this run measured. The notes cover the low figures whose reason we know.
benchmarksPerCountry.caption: Response rate, latency and completeness per country

benchmarksNotes.DE: No German register can be queried by VAT number: only the Peppol directory answers, and it holds about 12 700 German participants.
benchmarksNotes.ES: Spain discloses neither name nor address through VIES: both come back as “---”, so only validity is meaningful.
benchmarksNotes.IE: The Irish address carries no postal code to split it on, so postal code and city stay empty.
benchmarksNotes.PL: The White List publishes the address as a single string: no postal code, no city.
benchmarksNotes.LV: The Latvian register ships one address string and a territory code rather than a named city.

versus.title: {{siteName}} vs VIES · {{siteName}}
versus.description: {{siteName}} and VIES asked about the same VAT numbers in the same second: response time, how often a question got an answer, and how much of a company record comes back.
versus.lead: Every VAT number looked up twice in the same second: once through {{siteName}}, once straight at VIES. Here are the results.
versus.error: The comparison figures could not be loaded.
versus.noscript: The figures are read from a JSON file, so this page needs JavaScript.
versus.invalid: This comparison did not run to the end: {reason}. The figures below are incomplete and are shown for information only.

versusPerCountry.title: Country by country
versusPerCountry.lead: Best first. {{siteName}} answers from a national register wherever one is open to it, and asks VIES everywhere else, which is why some countries pull away and others sit level. The error rate is the share of requests that got no answer at all; a register stating the number is not registered has answered. Completeness asks two questions of each request: can the company be named, and can it be located. It is counted over every request made, including the ones that came back with no record.
versusPerCountry.caption: Response time and completeness per country, {{siteName}} against VIES, best first

versusMethod.title: How this was measured
versusMethod.paired: For each VAT number we make two requests a fraction of a second apart, and we alternate which one goes first. Comparing two test runs made on different days would let a bad day at VIES pass for a flaw in the product; asking both at the same moment removes that risk.
versusMethod.baselineTitle: VIES exactly as you would get it
versusMethod.baseline: The VIES side is one request, asked once. {{siteName}} asks again when a country replies that it is busy, stops asking a country it has just seen fail, and can serve the last answer it holds. That is the work you would otherwise have to do yourself. Waiting and asking again takes longer than giving up, so on a country that is down {{siteName}} is the slower of the two, and the one that comes back with an answer. Both sides name the same requester and therefore make the same call to VIES, the one that comes back with a consultation number.

versusBeyond.title: A question VIES does not answer
versusBeyond.lead: Speed and completeness can be measured. The complete report has no equivalent on the VIES side.
versusBeyond.text: VIES gives you its own opinion and nothing else. Every source at once asks, in a single call, every source that country has: the national register we hold, the register's own live endpoint where it publishes one, and VIES. Each comes back with its verdict and its date, and a line says so when it did not answer. No source is left out because a faster one already replied.

account.title: My account
account.lead: Everything this account holds, and what can be done with it.
account.deleteLead: Erasing your account is your right, and it is not reversible. Read what happens before you type anything.
account.deleteWhatGoes: Your email address, your billing details and your API keys are removed from the active database immediately. Every key stops answering within a minute, and any integration still calling the API will start receiving 401.
account.deleteWhatStays: Invoices already issued are kept for their legal period in restricted archive, and logs until their published retention period ends. Usage counters are kept without anything identifying you.
account.deleteConfirmPrompt: This erases your account and stops every API key. There is no undo. Continue?
account.deleteBlockedPaid: Your Pro subscription is still running. Cancel it from the Billing page first: we will not delete an account Stripe is still billing. This is a constraint of this button only: your right to erasure under Article 17 GDPR can be exercised at any time by writing to {{email}}, and we will handle the cancellation ourselves.
account.deleteMismatch: The confirmation word did not match. Nothing was deleted.
account.deleteDoneLead: Your personal data has been removed from the active database and your API keys no longer work. What the law requires us to keep stays in restricted archive until its retention period ends. Thank you for having used Vatlas.

data.title: Personal data
data.lead: Everything Vatlas holds about you, why we hold it, and what you can do about it.
data.tierPersonalLead: Data about you as a person, in the sense Article 4(1) GDPR gives the word: it identifies you, or it says something about you. This is what the right of access is for.
data.tierAccountLead: Contractual and technical: what you bought, what you spent, what your integrations are. It becomes personal data only because it hangs off an account we can put a name to. It is shown because it is yours, not because the Regulation compels it.
data.tierOthersTitle: Data about the companies you looked up
data.tierOthersLead: Not data about you. The vast majority of it concerns legal persons, which the GDPR does not cover; a record concerning a sole trader is personal data belonging to that person, not to you, and section 11 of the Privacy Policy answers for it. It is here because you asked for it and it is kept on your account.
data.andMore_one: and {{n}} more, carried in full by the exports.
data.andMore_other: and {{n}} more, carried in full by the exports.
data.eraseConfirm: Delete everything under “{{section}}”? This cannot be undone.
data.eraseBlockedPaid: Your billing details cannot be deleted while a subscription is running: an invoice has to be issued to an address. Cancel the subscription from the Plan page first, or write to us and we will handle both.
data.exportLead: Everything on this page and everything behind it, including the categories not shown: the record of our servers calling yours, and your callback settings. Article 20 GDPR.
data.exportNote: Both files carry the same thing in the same words: the API's own field names, in English, whatever language you read the console in. A field called vatNumber in one and something else in the other would be two exports of two different things. Collections are capped at {{cap}} rows, and each says how many exist. Your secret keys and your callback signing secret are deliberately not in them.
data.rightsLead: This page is where most of them are exercised. The rest is one email away.
data.rightAccess: Access. This page is the answer: every category above is what we hold, read from the live database at the moment you loaded it.
data.rightRectify: Rectification. Each category names the page that writes it, so a value is corrected where it was entered.
data.rightErase: Erasure. Category by category, with the button under each one that can offer it honestly, and the whole account on the account page. Where a category has no button, it says which obligation stands in the way.
data.rightPortability: Portability. The two exports above, in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format.
data.rightObject: Objection and restriction. They apply to what we hold on our legitimate interest: the security logs and the technical call logs above. Write to us and we will act on it.
data.rightComplain: Complaint. You may lodge one with the CNIL, the French data protection authority, at any time and without asking us first.
data.identityWhy: The address is the account: it is how you log in, where password resets go, and where invoices and service notices are sent. Without it there is no account to hold anything else.
data.identityKeep: For as long as the account exists. An account left unused for three years is erased automatically, a month after a warning email.
data.identityUse: Signing you in, writing to you in your own language, and applying the quota your plan allows. No profiling, no advertising, no automated decision about you, and never sold or shared.
data.identityNoErase: The address cannot go on its own: it is what the account is. Erasing it means erasing the account.
data.consentWhy: Which version of the Terms you accepted, when, and from which IP address. The Terms undertake to keep that on record and to provide it on request; this is the record.
data.consentBasis: Performance of the contract, and our legal obligation to be able to demonstrate what was agreed.
data.consentKeep: For as long as the account exists, and then for as long as a dispute about the contract can still be raised.
data.consentUse: Nothing routine reads it. It is evidence, consulted only if what you agreed to is ever in question.
data.consentNoErase: It is the proof of the contract between us, and erasing it would erase your evidence as much as ours.
data.billingWhy: The name and address an invoice is issued to, and the VAT number that applies the reverse charge. Filled in only if you subscribe. These are personal data when you trade in your own name: the company name is then your name, and the address may be your home; for a company they are a legal person's, which the GDPR does not cover.
data.billingBasis: Performance of the contract, and legal obligation for the invoices issued from it.
data.billingKeep: For as long as the account exists. An invoice already issued keeps its own copy for the ten-year accounting period, in restricted archive, which deleting this does not reach.
data.billingUse: Issuing invoices, and deciding whether VAT applies to your subscription. If you asked for it to be autofilled, it was resolved by the same public-register lookup the API performs.
data.paymentWhy: The identifiers Stripe knows you and your subscription by, and the state it is in. No card number ever reaches us: those are entered on Stripe's own pages.
data.paymentKeep: For as long as the subscription runs, and then with the accounting records that follow it.
data.paymentUse: Opening your invoices in Stripe's Customer Portal, and granting or dropping the Pro plan when Stripe says the subscription changed.
data.paymentNoErase: Written by Stripe's webhook, not by hand. Cancel the subscription and the record follows it; it is cleared when the account is erased.
data.keysWhy: One key per integration, so that a call can be attributed to whatever made it and one integration can be cut off without stopping the others.
data.keysKeep: For as long as the account exists, revoked keys included: the calls already made keep a name to hang off.
data.keysUse: Authenticating every API call and counting it against your monthly quota. The secret itself is shown on the keys page and is deliberately absent from both exports.
data.keysNoErase: A key is revoked rather than deleted, on the keys page, and stops answering within a minute.
data.sessionsWhy: One row per browser signed in, with the IP address and the browser it announced. It is what lets you tell your own sign-ins from somebody else's.
data.sessionsBasis: Performance of the contract for staying signed in; legitimate interest in securing the account for the IP address and the browser.
data.sessionsKeep: A session ends after thirty days without use. The row is then kept twelve months as a security log.
data.sessionsUse: Keeping you signed in, and investigating an incident on the account afterwards. The session token is stored as a one-way fingerprint, never in clear.
data.linksWhy: Every email verification and password reset link asked for, with the IP address that asked. It is what makes a link single-use, and what limits how many can be requested for one address.
data.linksBasis: Performance of the contract, and legitimate interest in not letting our mail be turned on somebody else's inbox.
data.linksKeep: A reset link expires in thirty minutes, a verification link in twenty-four hours. The row is kept twelve months after that, as a security log.
data.linksUse: Proving the address and resetting the password, once per link, and throttling the requests. The token is stored as a one-way fingerprint, exactly as a session is.
data.signinsWhy: Every wrong password typed for this account, with the IP address it came from. A successful sign-in clears them.
data.signinsBasis: Legitimate interest in protecting the account against password guessing.
data.signinsKeep: Thirty days, then deleted. A successful sign-in deletes them at once.
data.signinsUse: Locking the account for a quarter of an hour after five failures in a row, and investigating an incident on the account afterwards.
data.callbacksWhy: Where Monitor events and finished asynchronous lookups are sent when they name no address of their own, and the secret every callback we send is signed with.
data.callbacksBasis: Performance of the contract: you gave us the address so that we would call it.
data.callbacksKeep: For as long as you keep them. They are a standing instruction, not a record of anything.
data.callbacksUse: Sending your callbacks, and signing them so your endpoint can verify they came from us. Deleting them stops delivery for every monitor and every lookup relying on the default rather than naming a URL of its own.
data.monitorsWhy: The companies you asked to be told about, where to tell you, and what we last told you. A standing instruction you wrote.
data.monitorsKeep: For as long as you keep the monitor. It goes when you stop following the company, and when the account is erased.
data.monitorsUse: Checked against the registers regularly; a change sends you a callback. The numbers followed are used for nothing else and are never resold.
data.monitorsNoErase: Stopped one at a time on the Monitor page, so ending one does not end the rest.
data.asyncWhy: The numbers you queued when a source was down, where the result had to go, and the answer we ended up with.
data.asyncKeep: Ninety days from the day it finished. One still being retried is kept until it answers or is given up on, which is at most a week.
data.asyncUse: Retried until a source answers, then delivered to your callback URL. The stored answer is the same envelope the synchronous call would have returned.
data.deliveriesWhy: Every callback we sent you: the address called, what was in it, and what your endpoint answered. It exists so that you can debug your own receiver.
data.deliveriesKeep: Ninety days. A payload carries a company's name and address, and nobody debugs against a request from last winter.
data.deliveriesUse: Shown to you on the Monitor and Lookup Async pages, and read to send a failed delivery again. Nothing else reads it.
data.auditWhy: What the API answered, kept as it was sent, so that you can show months later what we told you about a business partner on the day you relied on it.
data.auditKeep: {{days}} days on the Pro plan; on the Free plan, your last {{free}} answers only, everything older deleted every night. Deleted outright when the account is.
data.auditUse: Read back by you, on the audit pages and over the API. It holds VAT numbers of other companies, kept only because you asked about them: nothing else reads it, and it is never resold.
data.usageWhy: One row per month: how many calls were billed against the quota, and the quota that applied at the time. It is what the dashboard chart draws.
data.usageBasis: Performance of the contract, and legal obligation where it supports an invoice.
data.usageKeep: For as long as the account exists. It is a month and two numbers: no VAT number and nothing about who was looked up.
data.usageUse: Enforcing the monthly quota, drawing your usage history, and settling a billing dispute.
data.usageNoErase: It enforces the quota you are on and supports the invoices issued for it, and it carries nothing beyond a month and a count.
data.logsWhy: One row per API call: when it was made, which number, which status, how long it took and which register answered. It is our instrumentation, and the record a billing dispute is settled from.
data.logsBasis: Legitimate interest in operating and securing the service; performance of the contract for the quota it enforces.
data.logsKeep: Ninety days, which covers the current month and the one before it, the window a dispute over a monthly quota can reach into. Past that only the aggregate counter survives.
data.logsUse: Measuring which countries are slow, showing per-key usage on your dashboard, and preventing abuse. It is not listed row by row, here or in the exports: it is our own instrumentation, and a count is the honest answer to what it holds about you.
data.logsNoErase: It is what a quota and a billing dispute are settled from, and it ages out on its own ninety-day window.
data.signinsNoErase: They are what locks the account against someone guessing its password, and erasing them would lift that lock. They age out on their own after thirty days, and a successful sign-in clears them.
